summary:
H.R. 8580, the “Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025,” makes FY2025 discretionary and advance appropriations for military construction, Department of Veterans Affairs programs, and related agencies, with specified periods of availability and numerous transfer, reprogramming, reporting, and use limitations.

Title I appropriates Department of Defense military construction and family housing funds, generally available through September 30, 2029, including Army ($2.218 billion), Navy and Marine Corps ($4.332 billion), Air Force ($3.268 billion), Defense-Wide ($3.500 billion, with transfer authority), National Guard and Reserve construction accounts, the NATO Security Investment Program ($433.864 million, until expended), the Department of Defense Base Closure Account established under section 2906(a) of the Defense Base Closure and Realignment Act of 1990, family housing construction and operation accounts, and the Family Housing Improvement Fund and Military Unaccompanied Housing Improvement Fund under 10 U.S.C. 2883. Sections 101–133 impose construction contracting, land acquisition, foreign contracting, notification, transfer, and obligation rules; permit specified transfers including to housing improvement funds, the Homeowners Assistance Program fund under 42 U.S.C. 3374, and “Foreign Currency Fluctuations, Construction, Defense”; appropriate Ford Island Improvement Account balances under 10 U.S.C. 2814; provide additional amounts for unfunded priority list projects, laboratory facilities, disaster-related Air Force expenses, child development centers, barracks, and demolition; and prohibit use of funds to close or realign Naval Station Guantanamo Bay.

Title II funds VA benefit, health, construction, administration, and cemetery accounts, including advance FY2026 appropriations for Compensation and Pensions ($204.482 billion), Readjustment Benefits ($17.614 billion), and major Veterans Health Administration accounts: Medical Services ($75.039 billion), Medical Community Care ($34 billion), Medical Support and Compliance ($12.7 billion), Medical Facilities ($9.7 billion), and the Cost of War Toxic Exposures Fund under 38 U.S.C. 324 ($22.8 billion). It also appropriates for VBA operations, IT systems, the Veterans Electronic Health Record, the Office of Inspector General, major and minor construction under 38 U.S.C. chapter 81, and state extended care and cemetery grants. Sections 201–261 authorize specified transfers among VA accounts; require quarterly financial, claims, EHR, and other reports; govern combined DOD-VA medical facility transfers and repeal section 220 of title II of division A of Public Law 118-42; restrict certain abortion-related funding subject to rape, incest, and life-endangerment exceptions; restrict gender-affirming surgical procedures and hormone therapies; limit canine, feline, and non-human primate research and require elimination by March 9, 2026; and supersede section 237 of division J of Public Law 117-328 regarding Social Security number authentication.

Title III appropriates for the American Battle Monuments Commission, the United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims, Army cemeterial expenses and Arlington construction, and the Armed Forces Retirement Home, and appropriates 10 U.S.C. 7727 special account deposits. Title IV contains government-wide limitations, including restrictions on transfers, lobbying, pornography on networks, first-class travel, Guantanamo detainee facilities, specified executive orders and DEI activities, certain VA procurement involving China, VA NICS reporting, marijuana-program form restrictions, and other VA-specific funding prohibitions.
